posts.title: 48 Bottles, One Sweep: How We Shot the Alder & Moss Range in a Day
posts.excerpt: Founder Ines Calloway explains how our Bay A crew planned, lit, and captured forty-eight skincare bottles in a single seven-hour packshot day.
posts.content:
When Alder & Moss came to Kirinuki Studio with forty-eight skincare bottles, they were facing a familiar e-commerce challenge. Their autumn product launch was only a few weeks away, and their online storefront needed consistent, high-key catalogue imagery across every SKU. Every bottle had to sit on a seamless white sweep with identical lighting ratios, controlled glass reflections, and natural ground contact shadows. Rather than stretching the commission over multiple days or outsourcing cut-outs to third-party services, we scheduled the entire collection for a single packshot day in Bay A.

Our studio day at Unit 4, Wharf Yard begins at 08:30 for equipment staging and crate load-in, with cameras rolling promptly at 09:00. For Alder & Moss, preparation had started two working days earlier during our shot-list call with studio manager Theo Mbeki. Theo verified bottle heights, grouped the formulations by glass opacity, and confirmed two clean camera angles for each piece: an eye-level hero front shot and a three-quarter perspective. Having this exact sequence mapped out before arrival allowed lead photographer Dev Raman and digital tech Marta Okonkwo to establish an efficient production tempo from the first frame.

Bay A is engineered specifically for high-volume commercial batch work. It houses our permanent six-metre white sweep alongside a counterweighted strobe and softbox overhead rig. Glassware is notoriously sensitive to minor shifts in studio environment, as curved glass surfaces mirror every stray stand and reflector in the room. Dev positioned a large rectangular softbox overhead and built a gentle side diffusion wall to carve clean, continuous highlight lines down the cylindrical shoulders of each bottle. Because the range featured both frosted glass and clear amber vessels, Marta calibrated custom exposure profiles to preserve the true hue of each serum without washing out subtle amber undertones.

The core of our studio practice is tethered capture with real-time review. As Dev released the shutter, each RAW file appeared instantaneously on Marta's thirty-two-inch calibrated colour monitor. This live feedback loop eliminates the uncertainty that so often plagues commercial shoots. Instead of waiting days to discover a tilted label or an errant reflection, our crew approved every first frame on screen right beside the physical product. When a label needed micro-alignment, Marta stepped in with tweezers and cotton gloves, Dev fired a confirmation frame, and the batch moved onward.

By 16:30, thirty minutes ahead of our 17:00 wrap, all ninety-six frames—two angles across forty-eight individual bottles—were locked, backed up locally, and logged in our system. Because every day rate at Kirinuki Studio includes our seven standard commitments, Alder & Moss knew exactly what would follow. Our retouch lead, Noor Petrova, managed surface dust clean-up, calibrated final colour fidelity against our physical swatch cards, and prepared export crops tailored to their online marketplace dimensions.

True to our studio turnaround rules, the complete online review gallery was delivered in three working days. Alder & Moss signed off on the hero selection with zero revision requests, and their final high-resolution retouched assets were delivered within five working days. The resulting imagery provided Alder & Moss with an elegant, unified catalogue ready for their autumn rollout. For Ines Calloway and the Kirinuki crew, it was another demonstration of how disciplined studio craft and clear communication turn complex product inventories into calm, consistent visual clarity in a single working day.
